items.title: Optical networking firm Lumilens valued at $5.5 billion in latest funding round
items.summary: Optical networking startup Lumilens said on Thursday it was valued at $5.51 billion in its latest funding round, ‌as surging investment in AI data centers fuels demand for ‌high-speed connectivity technologies.  The San Jose, California-based company designs and manufactures optical and networking products ​that help data centers move data faster while using less power.  It raised more than $700 million in the Series C funding round co-led by Atreides Management, Bain Capital Ventures, Meritech, Seligman Ventures and Spark Capital, bringing its ‌total funding to more than $900 ⁠million.

items.title: Could Microsoft, Amazon, or Google Actually Buy Reddit?
items.summary: Reddit sits at the intersection of AI training data, social commerce, and authentic human conversation, making it one of the most strategically valuable assets on the internet right now. But super-voting insiders hold the real power, and the list of buyers capable of clearing that bar is shorter than you might expect.

items.title: The Netflix Shock Reveals Which ETF Structure Protects You Better in a Downturn
items.summary: Netflix shares dropped sharply after its Q2 earnings, but three popular ETFs that all hold the stock reacted in surprisingly different ways. The structure of each fund tells you far more about your real risk than the name on the label.

items.title: Exclusive: Mirendil inks $100M+ Google Cloud deal to scale self-improving AI
items.summary: Mirendil has signed a $100 million-plus Google Cloud partnership to expand its compute infrastructure, powering research into self-improving AI systems designed to accelerate scientific discovery and AI development.

items.title: Alphabet taps bond market for up to $25 billion in 10-part sale
items.summary: Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL) is hitting the U.S. corporate debt market with a massive 10-part benchmark bond sale, capitalizing on its pristine credit ratings to lock in capital as the tech giant rapidly scales its infrastructure. Expected to price today, Alphabet is seeking to raise as much as $25 billion from the offering, according to Bloomberg News. items.title: Alphabet seeks up to $25 billion from its latest bond sale, Bloomberg News reports
items.summary: Alphabet is looking to raise as much as $25 billion from its latest U.S. bond offering, Bloomberg News reported ‌on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter, weeks after the ‌tech giant's 2026 capital spending outlook triggered a steep selloff.  The maturities on the notes range from two to 40 years, Bloomberg reported.  Alphabet did not immediately comment on the ‌size of the offering.
